I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so at the start of the growing season I will keep to the pattern that fits my land, water, and labor best: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That is the system I trust most because it matches the local climate, uses the full year, and gives me stable grain for income and household security. I do not want to spread my land across many crops, because that makes fieldwork, irrigation, and pest control harder for me to manage. I will use improved seed for wheat because it is steady and familiar, and hybrid seed for maize because I care about stronger yield in summer. For tillage, I will plough before wheat to set up a good seedbed, then use rotary tillage before maize so I can turn the field around quickly after wheat harvest. I will apply moderate fertilizer, with more nitrogen on maize than wheat, because maize responds strongly and wheat still needs balanced feeding with phosphorus and some potassium. I will irrigate wheat more often since it grows through the dry spring, and maize fewer times because it can use summer rain. I will spray only as much as needed to control the common diseases, insects, and weeds that usually come here. My goal is not to chase the highest possible yield with high cost, but to keep a reliable, manageable plan that fits my conditions and reduces risk.
